definition: to happen, especially without being planned or expected

collocations.example: Most road accidents occur at night on busy highways.
Major changes occur in the body during adolescence.

definition: the tenth month of the year, after September and before November

collocations.example: The new semester usually begins in early October.
We expect the first frost in late October.

definition: a person who holds a position of authority in an organization or government

collocations.example: A senior government official confirmed the news to reporters.
Local officials approved the plan for the new road.

definition: a round vegetable with a strong smell and taste, used in cooking

collocations.example: We ordered a plate of crispy onion rings.
She garnished the soup with chopped spring onions.

definition: to control the way a machine or system works

collocations.example: Workers must be trained to operate heavy machinery safely.
The new software is simple and easy to operate.

definition: a belief or judgment about something, not based on fact

collocations.example: Public opinion gradually turned against the proposed tax increase.
We should seek expert opinion before making a decision.

definition: a situation or time when it is possible to do something you want

collocations.example: The company offers excellent job opportunities for young graduates.
She seized the opportunity to study abroad for a year.

definition: to disagree with and try to prevent something, such as a plan

collocations.example: Many residents strongly oppose the construction of the airport.
Local groups oppose the plan to build a factory.

definition: on the other side; facing or moving away from something

collocations.example: The two cars drove off in opposite directions.
The bank is on the opposite side of the street.

definition: one of the things you can choose in a particular situation

collocations.example: Taking the train is the best option for commuters.
Please review all available options before signing the contract.

definition: normal and not special or unusual in any way

collocations.example: The museum tells the stories of ordinary people.
It started out as a perfectly ordinary working day.

definition: to plan and arrange an event or activity

collocations.example: She offered to organize a meeting with the clients.
Volunteers helped organize the annual charity fundraising event.

definition: existing at the beginning; first, before any changes

collocations.example: The original plan was changed due to budget cuts.
The original version of the document has been lost.

definition: apart from the thing just mentioned; in other respects

collocations.example: A single lamp lit the otherwise empty room.
The two otherwise identical cars differ only in color.

definition: the part of a cooker, used for baking or roasting food

collocations.example: Preheat the oven before you put the cake in.
She reheated the leftovers in the microwave oven.

definition: to need to pay money back to someone you borrowed from

collocations.example: I still owe money to the bank for my car.

definition: a round metal container used for cooking food on a stove

collocations.example: Heat some oil in a large frying pan.
She put a pan of water on the stove.

definition: a sudden strong feeling of fear that prevents clear thinking

collocations.example: He suffered a panic attack before the job interview.
She searched for her keys in a complete panic.

definition: one of two or more people who own a business together

collocations.example: He started the company with his business partner.
She was made a senior partner at the accounting firm.

definition: a small area that is different from what is around it

collocations.example: The dog has a bald patch on its leg.
A small patch of blue sky appeared through the clouds.

definition: a track made or built for people to walk along

collocations.example: A winding path led up to the old house.
We followed a narrow path through the dense forest.

definition: a person who is receiving medical treatment from a doctor

collocations.example: The hospital is committed to excellent patient care.
Doctors treated the patient for a serious infection.

definition: a regular way in which something happens or is done

collocations.example: All three attacks followed exactly the same pattern.
Her sleeping habits fell into a regular pattern.

definition: a short period of time when you stop before continuing

collocations.example: There was a long pause before she finally answered.
An awkward pause followed his rather strange question.

definition: a situation in which there is no war or fighting

collocations.example: The organization works hard to promote world peace.
The two nations finally signed a lasting peace treaty.

definition: an instrument used for writing or drawing with ink

collocations.example: He signed the letter with an expensive fountain pen.
Could I borrow a pen to fill this out?

definition: money paid regularly to someone who has stopped working, usually because of age

collocations.example: She lives mainly on her state pension now.
The company manages a large pension fund for employees.

definition: for each; used when giving rates, prices, or measurements

collocations.example: The tour costs fifty dollars per person.
The workers are paid fifteen dollars per hour.

definition: one part in every hundred

collocations.example: Only ten percent of the students passed the exam.
I am one hundred percent sure about my answer.

definition: to do a task, duty, or action, often a difficult one

collocations.example: The robot can perform the same task repeatedly.
Employees must perform their duties with great care.

definition: a length of time with a beginning and an end

collocations.example: The project will last over a long period of time.
New employees must complete a three-month trial period.

definition: an animal that you keep at home for company or pleasure

collocations.example: Their children begged them for a pet dog.
I bought some fish food at the pet shop.

definition: relating to the body rather than the mind

collocations.example: Regular physical activity is good for your heart.
He tends to avoid all physical contact with strangers.

definition: a large musical instrument played by pressing black and white keys

collocations.example: She learned to play the piano as a child.
A beautiful grand piano stood in the corner.

definition: a baked dish of fruit or meat covered with pastry

collocations.example: She baked a delicious apple pie for dessert.
We bought a hot meat pie from the bakery.

definition: a farm animal with a fat body, kept for its meat

collocations.example: They raise hundreds of animals on their pig farm.
A wild pig ran across the muddy field.

definition: a number of things lying on top of each other

collocations.example: Your letter got buried under a pile of papers.
He swept the leaves into a huge pile.

definition: a short thin piece of metal used for fastening things

definition: a tall tree with leaves like needles, that stays green all year

definition: of a pale red color

collocations.example: She wore a pretty pink dress to the party.
The walls were painted a soft pale pink.

definition: a tube through which liquid or gas can flow

collocations.example: The water pipe burst and flooded the kitchen.
Workers are repairing the underground gas pipe today.

definition: an area of ground marked out for playing sports such as football

collocations.example: The football pitch was too wet to play on.
The players ran onto the pitch before the match.

definition: a feeling of sadness for someone who is suffering

collocations.example: She took pity on the lost, hungry dog.
He helped them out of pity, not duty.

definition: simple and ordinary, without decoration or anything extra

collocations.example: He wore a plain white shirt to the interview.
She prefers plain water to sugary soft drinks.

definition: a vehicle with wings and engines that flies through the air

collocations.example: We traveled to Japan by plane last summer.
She booked a plane ticket to New York.

definition: a large round object in space that moves around a star

collocations.example: Planet Earth is the only known home of life.
Scientists discovered a distant planet orbiting another star.

definition: a light, artificial material that can be shaped when soft

collocations.example: She carried the groceries in a plastic bag.
These toys are cheaply made of hard plastic.

definition: a flat dish used for holding or serving food

collocations.example: She brought out a plate of warm cookies.
He filled his dinner plate with rice and vegetables.

definition: enjoyable, pleasing, or giving a feeling of satisfaction

collocations.example: We spent a pleasant day walking by the river.
Her early arrival was a very pleasant surprise.

definition: a feeling of happiness or enjoyment

collocations.example: She accepted the invitation with obvious pleasure.
He takes great pleasure in cooking for his friends.

definition: an object with pins used to connect a device to electricity

collocations.example: The electric plug does not fit this old socket.

definition: a small bag sewn into clothing for carrying small things

collocations.example: He kept the ticket in his coat pocket.
She slipped her phone into her back pocket.

definition: a piece of writing arranged in lines, often with rhythm or rhyme

collocations.example: She wrote a short poem about the ocean.
He read a beautiful love poem at the wedding.

definition: a person who writes poems

collocations.example: The museum honors a famous poet from this town.
She is widely admired as a gifted poet.

definition: a substance that can cause illness or death if swallowed

collocations.example: Some mushrooms contain a deadly poison.
They put out rat poison in the old barn.

definition: a long thin piece of wood or metal, usually standing upright

collocations.example: The truck crashed into a wooden telephone pole.
He cast his line using a long fishing pole.

definition: a set of plans or rules agreed by a government or organization

collocations.example: The president defended his new foreign policy today.
Our company policy does not allow personal phone calls.

definition: to rub the surface of something to make it smooth and shiny

collocations.example: He polished his shoes until they were shining.
She polished the wooden furniture every weekend.

definition: behaving in a way that is respectful and considerate of others

collocations.example: She greeted the guests with a polite smile.
They made polite conversation while waiting for the train.

definition: activities connected with governing a country or area

collocations.example: She decided to enter politics after her teaching career.
Voters are increasingly tired of party politics.

definition: to make air, water, or land dirty and unsafe to use

collocations.example: Factories that pollute the environment should pay heavy fines.
Chemical waste continues to pollute the local rivers.

definition: a large structure filled with water for swimming

collocations.example: The hotel has a large outdoor swimming pool.
We relaxed by the pool all afternoon.

definition: liked or enjoyed by many people

collocations.example: The new restaurant is very popular with tourists.
Soccer is the most popular sport in the country.

definition: the total number of people living in a particular area

collocations.example: The city is struggling to manage rapid population growth.
The country has a large and growing population.

definition: a place on the coast where ships load and unload

collocations.example: The town grew around a busy fishing port.
Shanghai is one of China's largest port cities.

definition: hopeful and confident, or focused on good qualities

collocations.example: She always keeps a positive attitude at work.
She kept a positive outlook throughout her long recovery.

definition: to have or own something

collocations.example: It is illegal to possess a weapon without a license.
She possesses all the skills needed for this job.

definition: a round vegetable that grows underground and is cooked before eating

collocations.example: The steak came with gravy and mashed potato.
She ordered a baked potato with melted cheese.

definition: to make a liquid flow from a container

collocations.example: Shall I pour the coffee now or later?
He poured water into the empty glass jug.

definition: relating to real situations and actions rather than ideas

collocations.example: The internship gave her valuable practical experience.
The theory has many useful practical applications.

definition: to do an activity repeatedly in order to improve a skill

collocations.example: If you practice speaking English daily, you will improve.
She practices the piano for an hour every evening.

definition: to speak to a god to give thanks or ask for help

collocations.example: They gathered to pray for the sick child.
She knelt down to pray to God quietly.

definition: to like one thing or person better than another

collocations.example: I would prefer to stay home this evening.
She prefers reading quietly to going out at night.

definition: having a baby developing inside the body

collocations.example: A pregnant woman should eat a healthy, balanced diet.
She was heavily pregnant with her second child.

definition: the elected leader of a republic or country

collocations.example: He was elected president by a narrow margin.
The former president gave a speech at the university.

definition: a feeling of stress caused by the need to do something

collocations.example: She performs well even under a lot of pressure.

definition: to think something is true because it is likely, without proof

collocations.example: The law presumes a person innocent until proven guilty.
You must be the new manager, I presume.

definition: to behave as if something is true when it is not

collocations.example: The children like to pretend to be superheroes.
He walked past and pretended not to notice me.

definition: to stop something from happening or existing

collocations.example: Heavy rain prevented them from finishing the game.

definition: happening or existing before the present time or event

collocations.example: Sales were much higher than in the previous year.

definition: a feeling of satisfaction from your own achievements or qualities

collocations.example: She takes great pride in her work.
He felt a deep sense of pride at graduation.

definition: most important, or of the best possible quality

collocations.example: This building is a prime example of modern design.

definition: to produce words or pictures on paper using a machine

collocations.example: Please print out a copy of the report.
I need to print this document before the meeting.

definition: the state of being free from public attention or interference

collocations.example: Reading someone's mail is a clear invasion of privacy.
The website claims it will protect your personal privacy.

definition: belonging to or for the use of one particular person or group

collocations.example: A sign warned visitors to keep off private property.
They reserved a private room for the business dinner.

definition: a series of actions taken in order to achieve a result

collocations.example: New technology has improved the entire production process.
Learning a new language is often a slow process.

definition: to make, create, or cause something to happen or exist

collocations.example: The dam produces electricity for the entire region.

definition: something that is made or grown to be sold

collocations.example: The company will launch a new product next month.
Customers increasingly care about product quality and safety.

definition: a type of job that needs special training or education

collocations.example: He is a lawyer by profession.
She has worked in the medical profession for years.

definition: the process of improving or getting closer to a goal

collocations.example: The students are making good progress in math.
The country is making steady progress in reducing poverty.

definition: a planned piece of work with a particular aim

collocations.example: She is leading an important research project this year.
Good project management keeps the team on schedule.

definition: to make the sound of a word or letter in a certain way

collocations.example: I don't know how to pronounce this long word.
Did I pronounce your last name correctly?

definition: a building or piece of land that someone owns

collocations.example: Prices in the property market have risen sharply.
They sold the valuable property for a huge profit.

definition: to suggest a plan or idea for others to consider

collocations.example: The committee proposed a plan to reduce traffic.

definition: a strong complaint or objection against something

collocations.example: Thousands joined the protest against the new law.
Several workers walked out in protest at the decision.

definition: feeling pleased about something you or others have achieved

collocations.example: They are very proud of their talented daughter.

definition: to show that something is true using facts or evidence

collocations.example: He argued loudly just to prove his point.

definition: to give something to someone who needs or wants it

collocations.example: The website provides useful information for new travelers.
The company provides employees with free health insurance.

definition: a place where people go to drink and meet friends

collocations.example: They met for a drink at the local pub.
We enjoyed a hearty pub lunch after the walk.

definition: a sweet dish eaten at the end of a meal

collocations.example: My grandmother makes delicious warm rice pudding.
We always eat Christmas pudding after the holiday meal.
